title: Structures, fluorescent properties and single-molecule-magnet behavior of two Ln (LnIII = Tb and Dy) clusters

synthesis.procedure: Tb(acac)3·2H2O (0.025 mmol) was dissolved in 20 mL of C2H5OH, then 5 mL CH2Cl2 solution of HL (0.025 mmol; HL = 5-((4-methylbenzylidene)amino)quinolin-8-ol) was added. The mixture was stirred for 5 h at room temperature, filtered, kept in the dark, and concentrated slowly by evaporation at room temperature. After about one week, yellow block crystals suitable for single-crystal X-ray diffraction were isolated.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution mixing, stirring, filtration, slow evaporation in the dark
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtered and kept in the dark; concentrated slowly by evaporation at room temperature; yellow block crystals isolated after about one week

properties.summary: Solid-state Tb(III) characteristic luminescence under 297 nm excitation. χMT(300 K) = 47.48 cm3 K mol−1, decreasing to 31.30 cm3 K mol−1 at 2.0 K (1.0 kOe). No significant out-of-phase ac signals under zero dc field; no SMM slow relaxation observed.

properties.summary: Solid-state Dy(III) emission at 481 and 575 nm (λex = 301 nm). χMT(300 K) = 56.94 cm3 K mol−1, decreasing to 36.10 cm3 K mol−1 at 2.0 K. Frequency-dependent ac susceptibility below 15 K with two χ″ maxima (slow and fast relaxation). High-T Orbach fit: ΔE/kB = 82.1 K, τ0 = 6.34×10−8 s; crossover to tunneling below 10 K. Cole–Cole α = 0.09–0.57 (2.0–15.0 K).
